complexity.correctness_reason: It computes 3Sum triples instead of the maximum container area: on heights=[1,7,2,5,4,7,3,6] it returns [] rather than 36.
complexity.notes: Wrong problem entirely: this is a 3Sum implementation (method named threeSum) pasted into max-water-container; the correct solution is a two-pointer scan moving the shorter side inward in O(n). Even as 3Sum it is poor: `x not in result` is a linear scan over up to O(n^2) tuples (use a set, which here hashes input-derived ints so average-case only), and it also misses duplicate-skipping logic and relies on List being imported.
complexity.summary: The submitted code solves 3Sum (sort + two-pointer sweep collecting triples that sum to zero), not Container With Most Water — it never computes any area. Within its own logic, it sorts, then for each anchor scans with two pointers, deduplicating via a linear `in` check on the result list, which is O(k) per match and drives the worst case to O(n^4).
